column2: The Bourbon government recognizes a Coptic-led Egyptian administration under its agreement with the Church. Coptic becomes the court's primary culture and the Coptic Christian tradition its state religion. Misri and Italian communities retain administrative recognition. This is a counterfactual political settlement: recognition of the Coptic Church does not make its Miaphysite doctrine Catholic.

The conditions of the Bourbon protectorate settlement no longer apply. The former administrative identity is restored where it was recorded. The people's cultures and religions have not been rewritten.
